forward_notes: r64 c15 IS NOT A LATENCY ORACLE AND SHOULD BE SPLIT. Its C1 is one conjunction -- status==200 AND cold AND duration_ms<5000 AND articles AND headlines==articles -- so a warm container fails it at 245 ms exactly as a cold 6-second one would, and the verdict token cannot tell an operator which happened. Worse, the cell is self-defeating on repetition: cold induction is ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) alone, so each run leaves exactly the 3 warm containers the next run needs, and a retry reads strictly worse than the first attempt (2 of 3 cold, then 0 of 3). Two clauses would fix it -- 'every cold sample is under 5 s' and 'at least N of 3 were cold' -- and then the halves could name the first one as the rollback trigger, which is what they already mean by 'c15 reads over 5 s'. Until then the cell has an undeclared PRECONDITION that belongs in the order: c15 must be the FIRST invoke after the apply, or after a measured invoke-free idle. ar-3 recorded a 900 s idle; this round graded the criteria first, read NO twice, and had to re-establish the idle (925 s) to get a gradeable read, which then passed 3 of 3 at 1945-2008 ms. The cost of getting this wrong is not a wasted read -- it is an executor staring at a named rollback trigger that has not actually fired, on a function whose real fault count is zero.

THE ORDER SHOULD STATE THE c15 SEQUENCING, not leave it to the executor to rediscover. Section 4's reported set lists c15 last in prose but the act of grading AC1-AC3 and the r64/r65/r66 set necessarily warms the function, so the written order and a correct c15 read are in direct conflict. One line -- 'take c15 FIRST, before any other deployed read, or after a 900 s invoke-free idle' -- removes the conflict.
